old_title: F1 Singapore GP LIVE: Race stream, updates and times with Verstappen leading
new_title: Lewis Hamilton despondent after making critical error in Singapore: 'I let you down'

Max Verstappen completed a superb Saturday around Singapore's shimmering streets as he backed up sprint victory with pole for Sunday's Grand Prix.
The Dutchman, who claimed his first race win of the season in last weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix held in Malaysia, continued to make strides forward in his improved Red Bull.
Verstappen was undone off the line in the sprint in damp conditions before George Russell crashed from the lead on lap one, the four-time world champion going on to complete a routine victory in the shortened dash.
Then, as he was 24 hours earlier, Verstappen was the class of the field in qualifying as he landed a first full Singapore pole. Charles Leclerc was just 0.054 seconds off the pace, pipping team-mate Lewis Hamilton - who will line up third ahead of runaway title leader Kimi Antonelli and McLaren's Lando Norris.
Follow live updates from the Singapore Grand Prix with The Independent
Charles Leclerc on team radio (Lap 12/62)
Leclerc: "I think plan C, opposite to Red Bull."
What are Ferrari thinking?
Leclerc is currently within two seconds of Verstappen, but Hamilton has dropped to around three seconds behind his teammate.
4-10: Antonelli, Norris, Piastri, Lawson, Hulkenberg, Gasly, Bearman
Audi car catches fire (Lap 10/62)
VSC ends pretty quickly as the car is wheeled into the pit-lane - but then it catches fire!
Pit-lane closed as the fire extinguishers do their thing... all fine.
VSC called (Lap 8/62)
Gabriel Bortoleto has stopped right by the pit-exit with a gearbox issue.
VSC deployed. Race neutralised, so to speak.
Not sure any of the frontrunners will pit... it's still very early.
Verstappen extends lead (Lap 7/62)
Verstappen, slowly but surely, is getting himself outside of the one-second window behind him.
Leclerc in second is around two seconds clear of Lewis Hamilton, while Kimi Antonelli is about 0.6 secs off the seven-time world champion.
At the back, George Russell has now got himself up to 14th. He's making steady progress.....
Leclerc right on Verstappen's gearbox (Lap 3/62)
Leclerc is not letting the Red Bull driver gallop down the road - the gap is just 0.6 seconds.
Where can he overtake, though?
Top-10: Verstappen, Leclerc, Hamilton, Antonelli, Norris, Piastri, Lawson, Hulkenberg, Gasly, Sainz
Verstappen keeps the lead!
Somehow, Verstappen keeps P1!
Charles Leclerc definitely got a better start and looked to be ahead going into turn one... but Verstappen held it around the outside!
The rest are all through clean - Hamilton in third, Antonelli in fourth.
Russell up to 17th in first lap or so...
Formation lap
Here we go then as Max Verstappen leads the pack around for the formation lap.
The pole-sitter is on soft tyres, as is Leclerc, while Hamilton is on mediums.
Russell at the back also on mediums.
Here we go then!
A reminder of the starting grid:
1. Max Verstappen (Red Bull)
2. Charles Leclerc (Ferrari)
3. Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari)
4. Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes)
5. Lando Norris (McLaren)
6. Oscar Piastri (McLaren)
7. Pierre Gasly (Alpine)
8. Liam Lawson (Racing Bulls)
9. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls)
10. Nico Hulkenberg (Audi)
11. Ollie Bearman (Haas)
12. Esteban Ocon (Haas)
13. Carlos Sainz (Williams)
14. Gabriel Bortoleto (Audi)
15. Franco Colapinto (Alpine)
16. Alex Albon (Williams)
17. Sergio Perez (Cadillac)
18. Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac)
19. George Russell (Mercedes)*
Pit lane. Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin)
Pit lane. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)
Pit lane. Isack Hadjar (Red Bull)
*Russell starts at the back of the grid due to an engine penalty
Singapore Grand Prix
Who's your money on, then?
Max Verstappen on pole has been the dominant driver this weekend as he looks to win the Singapore Grand Prix for the first time. If he gets off the line well, can anyone peg him back?
Ferrari in second and third with Leclerc and Hamilton - can they work together to earn a Scuderia win?
And what about the rest? Kimi Antonelli is in fourth, while George Russell is all the way at the back...

Lewis Hamilton apologised to his Ferrari team after making a strategic error which cost him a podium at the Singapore Grand Prix.
The seven-time F1 world champion started the race in third and looked well set for a podium behind race winner Max Verstappen and Ferrari teammate Charles Leclerc.
However, in contrast to the rest of the field, Hamilton pitted early for soft tyres and struggled towards the end of the race as his grip dropped off.
As such, in the closing stages, he lost three places to Kimi Antonelli, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri and was powerless to defend despite the Marina Bay Street Circuit's tight and twisty nature.
On team radio straight after the race, Hamilton revealed it had been his call and apologised to his Ferrari team: "Sorry boys, I let you down today with that strategy.
"It was my call and I lost us valuable points. I'll try and make up for it next time."
Hamilton, who had girlfriend Kim Kardashian watching in the Ferrari garage, was also permitted to not fulfil his post-race media sessions, as he was instead attended to by the FIA medical team.
The 41-year-old is now 111 points behind championship leader Antonelli, who can now win the world championship at the next round in Austin.
Verstappen is now fourth in the standings, just eight points off Hamilton, after claiming his second consecutive victory following his first triumph of the season last week in Malaysia.
